import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

# 1. Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv('reef.csv')

# 2. Bin trophic_level into 0.5-width categories
bins = np.arange(2.0, 5.0, 0.5)  # edges: [2.0,2.5,...,4.5]
labels = [f"{bins[i]:.1f}-{bins[i+1]:.1f}" for i in range(len(bins)-1)]
df['trophic_bin'] = pd.cut(df['trophic_level'], bins=bins, labels=labels, right=False)

# 3. Compute Shannon diversity per reef-year
#    Use 'quantity' as counts

def shannon_index(counts):
    freqs = counts / counts.sum()
    freqs = freqs[freqs > 0]
    return -np.sum(freqs * np.log(freqs))

group_cols = ['id_reef', 'year', 'protection_status']
shannon = (
    df.dropna(subset=['trophic_bin', 'protection_status'])
      .groupby(group_cols)
      .apply(lambda g: shannon_index(g.groupby('trophic_bin')['quantity'].sum()))
      .reset_index(name='shannon_div')
)

# 4. Subset to target statuses
subset = shannon[shannon['protection_status'].isin(['cabo pulmo', 'sin proteccion'])].copy()
subset['prot'] = subset['protection_status']

# 5a. Non-parametric test
group1 = subset.loc[subset['prot']=='cabo pulmo', 'shannon_div']
group2 = subset.loc[subset['prot']=='sin proteccion', 'shannon_div']
stat, pval = mannwhitneyu(group1, group2, alternative='two-sided')
print(f"Mann-Whitney U test: U={stat:.1f}, p-value={pval:.4f}")

# 5b. Mixed-effects model
tmp = subset.dropna(subset=['shannon_div'])
model = smf.mixedlm('shannon_div ~ C(prot)', data=tmp, groups=tmp['id_reef']).fit(reml=False)
print(model.summary())

# 6. Violin plot
plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
sns.violinplot(x='prot', y='shannon_div', data=subset, order=['cabo pulmo','sin proteccion'], inner='box')
plt.xlabel('Protection Status')
plt.ylabel('Shannon Diversity (trophic levels)')
plt.title('Trophic-level Shannon diversity by protection status')
plt.show()

messages.content: {"experiments":[{"hypothesis":"Reefs surveyed across two depth strata (shallow and deep) exhibit higher annual fish productivity per unit area than reefs surveyed in only a single depth stratum.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Test whether multi-strata reefs have greater mean annual productivity per 250 m² transect than single-stratum reefs.","steps":"1. For each reef–year, count the number of unique depth strata present (1 vs 2).  2. For each reef–year, sum the productivity across all transects and divide by total transect area (number of transects × 250 m²) to get productivity per m².  3. Label each reef–year as 'single-stratum' or 'multi-stratum'.  4. Compare the distribution of productivity per m² between the two groups using a t-test or a linear mixed‐effects model with group as a fixed effect and reef as a random intercept.  5. Check model assumptions (normality of residuals, homoscedasticity) and, if necessary, apply a transformation or use a nonparametric test.","deliverables":"1. Table of mean and standard deviation of productivity per m² for single vs multi-stratum reefs.  2. Statistical test output (test statistic, p-value, effect size).  3. Boxplot or violin plot showing productivity per m² by stratum count."}},{"hypothesis":"Across reef–years, the ratio of productivity to standing biomass (P/B) is negatively correlated with average fish size, indicating higher turnover in communities dominated by smaller fishes.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Assess the relationship between average fish size and the P/B ratio at the reef–year scale.","steps":"1. For each reef–year, compute total productivity and total biomass by summing those values across all observations.  2. Compute the P/B ratio = total productivity / total biomass.  3. Compute the average fish size per reef–year as the quantity-weighted mean of individual fish sizes.  4. Fit a linear regression or mixed‐effects model: P/B ~ avg_size + (1|reef).  5. Evaluate the strength and significance of the size coefficient, check residual diagnostics, and consider a log‐transformation if needed.","deliverables":"1. Dataframe of reef–year with avg_size, total biomass, total productivity, and P/B ratio.  2. Regression or mixed‐model summary (coefficients, R², p-values).  3. Scatterplot of P/B vs average size with fitted regression line."}},{"hypothesis":"Unprotected reefs exhibit higher inter-annual variability in species richness than strictly protected reefs, reflecting greater community instability under fishing pressure.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Compare the year-to-year variability of species richness between protected and unprotected reefs.","steps":"1. For each reef–year, list all species observed (presence) and compute species richness.  2. For each reef, calculate the coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) of richness across all surveyed years.  3. Label each reef by its predominant protection status (e.g., majority of years ‘cabo pulmo’ vs ‘sin proteccion’).  4. Compare CV distributions between protection statuses using a t-test or Wilcoxon test, or fit a linear model CV ~ protection_status.  5. Verify assumptions or use permutation testing if assumptions are violated.","deliverables":"1. Table of reef-level richness CV and protection status.  2. Statistical test or model output (effect size, p-value).  3. Bar chart or boxplot of CV of richness by protection status."}},{"hypothesis":"Species biomass evenness is lower in deep strata compared to shallow strata, indicating dominance by fewer species at depth.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Test whether biomass distribution among species is less even in deep transects than in shallow transects.","steps":"1. For each reef–year–depth combination, aggregate biomass by species.  2. Compute Shannon diversity H for biomass proportions and Pielou’s evenness = H / ln(S), where S is the number of species present.  3. Pair shallow and deep evenness values within the same reef–year.  4. Use a paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test to compare evenness between depths.  5. Optionally, fit a mixed‐effects model: evenness ~ depth + (1|reef–year).","deliverables":"1. Dataset of evenness by reef–year–depth.  2. Test results (test statistic, p-value, confidence interval).  3. Paired boxplot or connected-dot plot of evenness in shallow vs deep strata."}},{"hypothesis":"Protected reefs exhibit lower mean beta diversity among neighboring reefs within the same region compared to unprotected reefs, indicating greater community homogenization under protection.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Compare community dissimilarity (beta diversity) between pairs of reefs inside vs outside marine protection.","steps":"1. For each region–year, identify all reefs with the same protection status (protected or unprotected).  2. For each pair of reefs within that group, compile species presence–absence lists and compute Jaccard dissimilarity.  3. Calculate the mean Jaccard dissimilarity per region–year–status.  4. Compare mean beta diversity between protected and unprotected groups using a mixed‐effects model: beta_div ~ protection_status + (1|region).  5. Assess significance and check model diagnostics.","deliverables":"1. Table of mean beta diversity by region, year, and protection status.  2. Model output (fixed‐effect estimate, p-value).  3. Boxplot of pairwise Jaccard dissimilarities by protection status."}},{"hypothesis":"Reefs with lower initial biomass exhibit larger year-to-year increases in productivity, suggesting compensatory production at low biomass levels.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Determine if low-biomass reefs show greater gains in productivity over successive years.","steps":"1. For each reef and year, calculate total biomass and total productivity.  2. For each reef–year where year+1 data exist, compute biomass at time t and change in productivity = productivity_{t+1} − productivity_t.  3. Fit a linear mixed‐effects model: prod_change ~ biomass_t + (1|reef).  4. Examine the coefficient on biomass_t to see if it is significantly negative.  5. Validate model assumptions; consider log‐transforming variables if needed.","deliverables":"1. Dataset of biomass_t, productivity_t, productivity_{t+1}, and prod_change.  2. Model summary (coefficient, p-value).  3. Scatterplot of prod_change vs biomass_t with regression line."}},{"hypothesis":"Annual herbivore biomass is positively associated with the productivity of higher trophic levels at the reef scale, indicating bottom-up facilitation via grazing.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Test whether reefs with more herbivore biomass produce more biomass in higher trophic levels within the same year.","steps":"1. Classify observations as herbivores if trophic_level ≤ 2.5, and as higher trophic levels if trophic_level > 2.5.  2. For each reef–year, sum herbivore biomass and sum productivity of higher trophic observations.  3. Fit a linear model or mixed effects model: high_trophic_prod ~ herbivore_biomass + (1|reef).  4. Check for collinearity with total biomass and include as covariate if necessary.  5. Evaluate model fit and significance of herbivore biomass effect.","deliverables":"1. Reef–year dataset with herbivore_biomass, high_trophic_prod, total biomass.  2. Model output (coefficients, p-values).  3. Scatterplot of high trophic productivity vs herbivore biomass with fit line."}},{"hypothesis":"Reefs with a higher average proportion of large-bodied fish (>30 cm) exhibit greater inter-annual variability in their P/B ratios, reflecting unstable production dynamics in large-fish–dominated communities.","experiment_plan":{"objective":"Assess whether dominance by larger fishes is linked to more variable annual production-to-biomass ratios.","steps":"1. For each reef–year, sum biomass of observations with size > 30 cm and compute total biomass, yielding proportion_large = large_biomass / total_biomass.  2. Compute P/B ratio for each reef–year.  3. For each reef, calculate the standard deviation of its P/B ratios across years and the mean proportion_large.  4. Fit a linear regression: sd_PB ~ mean_proportion_large.  5. Test significance of the slope, plot diagnostics, and consider Spearman correlation if residuals are non-normal.","deliverables":"1. Reef-level table of sd_PB and mean_proportion_large.  2. Regression or correlation summary (slope, R² or ρ, p-value).  3. Scatterplot of sd_PB vs mean_proportion_large with fitted line or correlation annotation."}}]}
